extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy analysts, and users of WIPO patent statistics (IP office analysts, academics, government statisticians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and methodological notes for interpreting and using WIPO patent statistics (applications, grants, patent families, technology field mappings, and inventor gender attribution). Includes definitions, counting rules, and caveats about data comparability and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not compare applications and grants in same year
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination process can also be a lengthy one therefore there is a time lag between application and grant dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this reason, data on applications for a given year should not be compared with data on grants for the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of application origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent filing activity by origin includes resident applications and applications filed abroad. The origin of a patent application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states. See the glossary for the definition of equivalent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of regional office filings (equivalent application counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means filings at a regional office are treated as multiple (equivalent) applications for origin-based measures; consult the glossary for formal definition of 'equivalent application'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute counts vs equivalent counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin data are based on absolute counts, not equivalent counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful when comparing tables/figures: some series or tables use absolute counts while others (labelled 'equivalent') adjust for multiple filings across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a patent family
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families are defined as patent applications interlinked by one or more of the following: priority claim, Patent Cooperation Treaty national phase entry, continuation, continuation-in-part, internal priority and addition or division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent families here include only those associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude patent families associated with utility model applications. Applicants often file in multiple jurisdictions so inventions may be recorded more than once; patent-family-based indicators take account of this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-oriented patent families
rubrics_metrics.description: A special subset of patent families comprises foreign-oriented patent families: this includes only patent families that have at least one filing office different from the office of the applicant’s country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some foreign-oriented patent families include only one filing office because applicants may choose to file directly with a foreign office (example: a Canadian applicant filing directly with the USPTO without previously filing in Canada will form a foreign-oriented patent family with USPTO entries). Use this definition when measuring foreign-orientation or internationalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of utility model families from patent-family counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families include only those associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude patent families associated with utility model applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using family-based indicators note that utility model-related families are intentionally left out of the counts presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC-to-technology-field mapping (concordance table)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an electronic version of the IPC technology concordance table, visit www.wipo.int/ipstats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of IPC-based technology definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The correspondence between IPC symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence). It is therefore difficult to capture all patents in a specific technology field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even so, the IPC-based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority of patent applications in these areas. Use caution when interpreting narrow technology counts and consult annexes/definitions for specific technology mappings (e.g., fuel cells, geothermal, solar, wind).

rubrics_metrics.name: Published applications: 18-month publication delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications. There is a minimum delay of 18 months between the application date and the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication-based series therefore lag behind filing activity; take the 18-month minimum delay into account when analyzing time trends or recent activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin data for published vs equivalent counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent activity by origin includes resident applications and applications filed abroad; origin data shown in some tables are based on absolute counts rather than equivalent counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing 'top offices' tables with 'top origins' or 'equivalent' tables, confirm whether counts are absolute or equivalent to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender attribution methodology for inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: To attribute gender to inventors’ names recorded in PCT applications, WIPO produced a world gender–name dictionary based on information from 13 different public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender is attributed to a given name on a country-by-country basis because certain names may be considered male in one country but female in another. Users should recognise potential attribution errors and limitations of name-based gender inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on selected-office and region/income-group presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected offices are from different world regions and income groups (low-income, lower middle-income and upper middle-income).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available, data for all offices are presented in comprehensive tables (e.g., table A59). Use regional/income-group context when interpreting selected-office comparisons. '..' indicates data not available.
